anchors: xcl:MH_1_1_04_Faustos ed. page 413 - PDF page 137 (word id 56957) (w2/2)
near_miss.lead: ON 'sætr Olaf son sinn i kne seer' (mother sets son on her knee)
near_miss.why_not: Partners share only *ǵonu-: Hesiod has Sirius parching head and knees, the Armenian has a rider's knee not reaching the horse. Not a parallel; the real Homeric partners lie outside the slab (filed as a search lead).

near_miss.lead: ON 'ausit sveininn vatni' (pre-Christian water-sprinkling at naming) ~ Hom ἀφυσσάμενοι ὕδωρ / Lat haustus
near_miss.why_not: Different acts (sprinkling an infant vs drawing water for a ship/drinking); ἀφύσσω's link to *h2ews- is doubtful; water+draw is generic. The Irish thumb-under-tooth (ordain fa dét) vs ON tooth-gift (tonn) share only the tooth word, in unrelated contexts.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_2_11_Agathangelos ed. page 1561 - PDF page 267 (word id 46592) (w4/4)
xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 712 - PDF page 192 (word id 31589) (w1/3)
near_miss.lead: Njáls 'it sǿtasta ljós augna minna' (light of my eyes); 'see with one's eyes' (oculis uidi ~ видѣти очима ~ աչօք տեսանել); Arm. յականէ յանուանէ
near_miss.why_not: The light of the eyes is a Psalm idiom (lumen oculorum meorum), and the Agathangelos light is Ps 35:10, not the eyes. Seeing with one's own eyes is universal. ON 'kenna augu Olafs' is recognition by the eyes, not a phrase.

near_miss.lead: ON songr (sværða song) ~ Gk ὀμφή (θεοῦ ὀμφῇ), both o-grade *songʷʰ- + genitive
near_miss.why_not: A real cognate pair, but the frames do not match: a battle kenning 'song of swords' vs the oracular 'voice of the god'. Genitive + noun is no figure.

near_miss.lead: Law: father 'kvangar sun sín ok giptir dóttur sína' ~ Ru. Pravda 'а дчери можеть дати'; son/daughter pair sunr/dóttir ~ сынъ/дъчи
near_miss.why_not: The kin terms are basic vocabulary. 'Give a daughter' is universal and the verbs are not cognate (gipta vs дати). The contexts differ (a dowry provision vs a mother's estate).

near_miss.lead: Sleep/night: ON 'vaker um nottena', 'sofa ... hvíla sér nótt' ~ Hom ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον; ON hvíla ~ Lat quies (Catul. 'somnus ... quiete')
near_miss.why_not: The sleep, rest and night semantic field is generic. hvíla~quiēs is cognate but there is no shared construction. Herodotus' Gyges night plot has no cognate wording.

near_miss.lead: ON 'konungs nafn bera', 'bar æigi tignar namn' (bear a name = hold a rank)
near_miss.why_not: No slab partner has bher- + name: in the MBh 'bharata' is a vocative name and 'bindusaraḥ nāma' a naming formula, and the Irish 'a ainm' is not construed with do-beir. Vedic nā́ma bhr̥- found by search is filed as a search lead.

near_miss.lead: ON 'hæitum a almatkan guð' ~ RV 'ávase havāmahe' (guð < *ǵʰuH-tó- 'invoked' vs hū- 'call'); 'bera fé' ~ AV bibharṣi ... paśūnām; 'fótum fjǫr at launa'
near_miss.why_not: heita á guð is a Christian hagiographic idiom; its verb is not cognate with hū-, and the guð etymology is itself disputed. AV bibharṣi and paśūnām are not in construction. 'fótum fjǫr at launa' has no partner. Plautus' Trojan horse (BS-0a007) has nothing.

error.correct_reading: Finnr 'Finn, Sámi' (here a sorcerer, 'the Finn'), an ethnonym from Gmc *finnaz of uncertain etymology
error.evidence: Context: Olaf has 'the Finn' brought to him and asks whether he spoke the truth. No connection with *pes- 'penis'.

search_lead.cognate: ON setja (caus. *sod-éye-) ~ Gk ἕσσα/ἐφέσσεσθαι (*sed-s-), καθίσσας; ON kné ~ Gk γόνυ (*ǵónu); reflexive ON sér ~ Gk οἷσιν (*s(w)e-); OIr suidid fo glún (*sed-, *ǵnu-)
search_lead.argument: Setting a (dear) son on one's own knee, as a sign of acknowledging, rearing or fostering a child: Phoenix's father's curse that no dear son be set on his knees (Il. 9.455), and Phoenix setting the infant Achilles on his knees (Il. 9.488). In ON, Ásta sets her son Olaf on her knee before questioning him, and the knésetja motif recurs (Egils, Laxdæla, AM-36 Halfdan's sons). In OIr, Cú Chulainn sits under Conchobar's knee as his foster-son. The same verb root *sed-, *ǵonu- and a reflexive possessive in ON and Greek: a candidate for an inherited legitimation/fosterage gesture phrase. ON knésetja is also a legal-social practice, which could be cultural rather than linguistic inheritance. No Hittite parallel was found in the index.

search_lead.cognate: ON nafn ~ Ved. nā́man- (*h1nómn̥); ON bera ~ Ved. bhr̥- (*bʰer-)
search_lead.argument: 'Bear a name' meaning to hold an identity or status: ON 'konungs nafn bera', 'tignar nafn' (bear the title of king/rank), law 'bónda nafn berr'. The RV has Indra 'bearing a name to be praised / heard far off'. Exact cognates in the same verb-object frame. But the ON usage is chiefly in learned and legal prose (Konungs skuggsjá), where Latin nomen gerere/ferre may be the model, so inheritance is weak. Low.

note: Second reading of the 15 flagged bundles: no claims. The only promising leads (knee-setting of a son; bear a name) lack a matching slab partner and are filed as search leads.
